steps.title: 01-open: Open http://127.0.0.1:3000/ in the browser. If a login page appears, sign in with username admin and the password entered exactly as the text {{env:APP_PASSWORD}} (the environment fills in the real password when it is typed - type it exactly like that, do not alter or guess it). If Grafana prompts to change/skip updating the admin password after login, skip that step. Then find and open the provisioned dashboard named 'Service health' (use the Dashboards search/home page). Once it is open, report the exact titles of all the panels shown on that dashboard, in the order they appear.

02-create: In the same browser session (already signed in to Grafana at http://127.0.0.1:3000), create a NEW dashboard and add a panel of type 'Stat'. The panel must be titled '{{runid}} Availability' (runid {{runid}}). Its data source must be the 'TestData' data source (a test/random walk datasource). Make sure the panel renders a value (if the query needs any default, keep defaults). Then make sure the whole dashboard is properly SAVED (via the Save dashboard button, which is a real save, not just Apply/Back) with the dashboard title exactly '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard'. The dashboard title must be set to that exact value before saving - if a save dialog offers to set the name, set it there. Confirm the save succeeded (e.g. a 'Dashboard saved' toast) and report the saved dashboard's title and the panel title you see on the page.

03-open: In the same browser session, the saved dashboard '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard' (URL http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard) should be open. Add a NEW panel of type 'Text' titled '{{runid}} Notes'. Its text content must include the string '{{runid}}' (e.g. something like 'Notes for run {{runid}}'). Apply the panel edit, then perform a real Save of the dashboard (the Save dashboard button - not just Apply/Back). Verify the save persisted: reload the page and confirm the Text panel '{{runid}} Notes' is visible on the reloaded dashboard and its content contains {{runid}}. Report the panel title and a snippet of its text content as seen after reload.

04-open: In the same browser session, on the dashboard '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard' (http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard): (1) Open the dashboard settings (gear/Dashboard settings) and add the tag 'bench' to the dashboard's tags (manage tags so 'bench' is included), then save/apply settings. (2) Set the top-bar time range to 'Last 6 hours' (absolute range now-6h to now). (3) Perform a real save via the Save dashboard button, and in the save drawer make sure to tick the 'Update default time range' checkbox so the 6-hour range is persisted into the saved dashboard, then confirm/save. Verify persistence: reload the page and confirm the time picker shows 'Last 6 hours' on the freshly loaded page, and reopen dashboard settings to confirm the tag 'bench' is present. Report the tag(s) shown and the time range text after reload.

05-set: In the same browser session, on the dashboard '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard' (http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard): Set the dashboard's auto-refresh interval to '1m' (one minute). The refresh interval is configured in the dashboard settings under 'Auto refresh' — open Dashboard settings (gear), find the Auto refresh intervals option, and set the auto-refresh interval to 1m (add/ensure '1m' is in the intervals list if it's a list input, or select 1m). Apply/save the settings, then perform a real Save of the dashboard (Save dashboard button) if needed so it persists. Verify persistence: reload the page and confirm the auto-refresh shows 1m — check via the time picker's refresh menu (the Refresh button's dropdown should show 1m selected/available as auto refresh) or the settings page showing 1m. Report exactly what you observed after reload (e.g. the selected refresh interval text).

06-open: In the same browser session, on the currently open dashboard: verify and report (a) the exact current page URL shown in the browser's address bar (read it from the page, e.g. via location.href - do not guess), (b) the dashboard title shown in the breadcrumb/header, (c) the titles of all panels visible on the page in order, (d) the time picker's selected range text and the auto-refresh button's current interval text, and (e) open Dashboard settings and report the tags listed for this dashboard. Report each item exactly as observed.
